own_solution.law: SI unit conversion of power: 1 W = 1 J/s = 1000 mW = 0.001 kW
assumptions: The meter reading is taken at face value

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: The authors claim every rendering denotes the same power, but variant 2 states 0.22 kW (= 220 W) while the others state 200 W, so that rendering changes the value and not only the unit.
defect_reasons.failed_transformation_identity: The certified answer 200 W does not follow from variant 2 under the stated identity P = P_base with P_base = 200 W, because 0.22 kW converts to 220 W.

counterexamples: Variant 2: 0.22 kW * 1000 W/kW = 220 W, 10% above the certified 200 W.
notes: Agrees with pass 1. Variants 1, 3 and 4 (200 W, 200 J/s, 200000 mW) correctly convert to 200 W and match the certified answer; variant 2 should read 0.2 kW (or 0.20 kW). The governing 'equation' P = P_base is trivially dimensionally consistent. Even after the fix the item is a bare unit conversion with no physics content, so it would carry a naturalness flag.
